LESSON: WRITING POSTURE

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: WRITING
Topic 4.3: Writing Posture

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing Posture
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do we sit when Posture learners should be able to:the appropriate writing posture. writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. practise Writing Posture
2. use Writing Posture in clear sentences

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing Posture

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing Posture

Teach
• Focus skill: Writing Posture.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing Posture.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing Posture
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we sit when Posture learners should be able to:the appropriate writing posture. writing?
2. when • Learners could recite rhymes on the appropriate book when writing?
3. Where do we place our writing in class. • Learners could view a video clip demonstrating the left hand when writing?
4. Where do you place your class. could recite a writing posture rhyme as others feet while writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
